subtopics.name: Economics as a Science and Basic Concepts
objectives: Define economics and explain why it is a social science
Explain basic concepts: wants, scarcity, choice, scale of preference and opportunity cost
Apply the concept of opportunity cost to everyday decisions

subtopics.name: Basic Economic Problems of Society
objectives: Identify the basic economic problems: what, how and for whom to produce
Explain the production possibility curve and efficient resource allocation
Relate scarcity and choice to the basic economic problems

subtopics.name: Types of Economic Systems
objectives: Describe the features of capitalism, socialism and mixed economy
Compare the advantages and disadvantages of each economic system
Identify how basic economic problems are solved under each system

subtopics.name: Economic Systems in Africa and Nigeria
objectives: Explain why most African countries operate mixed economies
Explain the roles of the public and private sectors in a mixed economy

topics.name: Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis

subtopics.name: Scientific Approach and Basic Tools
objectives: Distinguish between positive and normative economics
Identify basic tools of economic analysis: tables, charts, graphs and equations
Interpret economic data presented in tables, bar charts, pie charts and graphs

subtopics.name: Measures of Central Tendency and Dispersion
objectives: Calculate and interpret the mean, median and mode of economic data
Calculate simple measures of dispersion (range, variance, standard deviation)
State the merits and demerits of each measure

subtopics.name: Demand: Concepts, Schedule and Curve
objectives: Define demand and state the law of demand
Construct demand schedules and demand curves
Distinguish between change in demand and change in quantity demanded
Identify the determinants of demand and types of demand (composite, derived, competitive, joint)

subtopics.name: Elasticity of Demand
objectives: Define and calculate price, income and cross elasticity of demand
Interpret elasticity values (elastic, inelastic, unitary)
Explain the importance of elasticity to consumers, producers and government

subtopics.name: Utility Theory
objectives: Define utility, total utility and marginal utility
Explain the law of diminishing marginal utility
Derive consumer equilibrium using the utility approach

subtopics.name: Indifference Curve Analysis
objectives: Explain the properties of indifference curves and budget lines
Determine consumer equilibrium using indifference curves
Explain the effects of income and price changes on consumer equilibrium

subtopics.name: Supply: Concepts, Schedule and Curve
objectives: Define supply and state the law of supply
Construct supply schedules and supply curves
Distinguish between change in supply and change in quantity supplied
Identify the determinants of supply and types of supply (joint, competitive, composite)

subtopics.name: Elasticity of Supply
objectives: Define and calculate price elasticity of supply
Identify factors affecting elasticity of supply
Explain the importance of elasticity of supply

subtopics.name: Equilibrium Price and Quantity
objectives: Explain how equilibrium price and quantity are determined by demand and supply
Calculate equilibrium price and quantity from schedules and equations
Explain the effects of shifts in demand and supply on equilibrium

subtopics.name: Price Control
objectives: Explain price ceiling (maximum price) and price floor (minimum price)
Analyse the effects of price control: surplus, shortage and black market
Explain minimum wage legislation and its effects

subtopics.name: Production: Concepts and Factors
objectives: Define production and identify its types (primary, secondary, tertiary)
Describe the factors of production (land, labour, capital, entrepreneurship) and their rewards
Explain division of labour and specialization with their advantages and disadvantages

subtopics.name: Production Functions and Returns
objectives: Explain the concepts of total, average and marginal product
State and illustrate the law of diminishing returns
Distinguish between returns to scale and internal/external economies of scale

subtopics.name: Cost Concepts
objectives: Distinguish between fixed cost, variable cost and total cost
Calculate average cost and marginal cost
Distinguish between accountant's and economist's notions of cost (explicit vs implicit)
Explain short-run and long-run cost behaviour

subtopics.name: Revenue Concepts and Profit
objectives: Define total revenue, average revenue and marginal revenue
Calculate revenues from given data
Determine break-even, profit and shut-down points

subtopics.name: Perfect Competition
objectives: State the features of a perfectly competitive market
Explain price determination and equilibrium of the firm under perfect competition
Distinguish between short-run and long-run equilibrium of the firm

subtopics.name: Imperfect Markets: Monopoly, Monopolistic Competition and Oligopoly
objectives: State the features of monopoly, monopolistic competition and oligopoly
Explain price and output determination under monopoly
Explain price discrimination and the control of monopoly
Compare market structures and their effects on consumers

subtopics.name: National Income Concepts and Measurement
objectives: Define national income concepts: GDP, GNP, NNP, national income per capita
Describe the income, output and expenditure approaches to measuring national income
Identify the problems of measuring national income in developing countries

subtopics.name: Uses and Determinants of National Income
objectives: Explain the uses of national income statistics and their limitations for comparing living standards
Explain the circular flow of income
Explain the concepts of consumption, savings, investment and the multiplier

subtopics.name: Money: Nature and Functions
objectives: Trace the evolution of money from trade by barter
State the characteristics and functions of money
Explain the demand for and supply of money and the value of money
Explain the quantity theory of money

subtopics.name: Inflation and Deflation
objectives: Define inflation and identify its types (demand-pull, cost-push) and causes
Explain the effects of inflation and measures to control it
Define deflation, its causes, effects and control

subtopics.name: Commercial Banks and Other Financial Institutions
objectives: Describe the functions of commercial banks and the process of credit creation
Identify other financial institutions: merchant banks, development banks, insurance companies, microfinance banks
Explain the roles of financial institutions in economic development

subtopics.name: The Central Bank and Monetary Policy
objectives: Describe the functions of the Central Bank of Nigeria
Explain the instruments of monetary policy (OMO, bank rate, reserve requirements, moral suasion)
Explain how monetary policy controls inflation and stimulates the economy

subtopics.name: Money and Capital Markets
objectives: Distinguish between money and capital markets and their instruments
Describe the functions of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
Explain the roles of money and capital markets in economic development

subtopics.name: Taxation
objectives: Define taxation and distinguish between direct and indirect taxes
Explain the principles/canons of taxation and tax systems (progressive, proportional, regressive)
Explain the incidence and effects of taxation

subtopics.name: Government Revenue, Expenditure and Budgets
objectives: Identify sources of government revenue and types of government expenditure
Explain types of budget (balanced, surplus, deficit) and their uses as fiscal policy tools
Explain public debt: types, reasons and effects
Explain revenue allocation and resource control in Nigeria

subtopics.name: Concepts of Growth and Development
objectives: Distinguish between economic growth and economic development
Identify indicators of development and characteristics of developing economies
Explain the problems of economic development in Nigeria

subtopics.name: Development Planning
objectives: Define development planning and state its objectives
Identify types of development plans and Nigeria's experience with planning
Explain the problems of development planning in Nigeria

subtopics.name: Role and Systems of Agriculture
objectives: Explain the contributions of agriculture to the Nigerian economy
Describe systems of agriculture (subsistence, commercial, plantation) in Nigeria
Explain the marketing of agricultural produce and the role of marketing boards

subtopics.name: Problems and Policies of Agriculture
objectives: Identify the problems of agriculture in Nigeria
Describe government agricultural policies and programmes and their effects
Explain the effects of agricultural price fluctuations on farmers' income

subtopics.name: Industrial Concepts and Location
objectives: Define industry, firm and plant and identify types of industries
Explain the factors influencing the location of industries in Nigeria
Explain localization of industries and its advantages and disadvantages

subtopics.name: Industrialization Strategies and Problems
objectives: Explain industrialization strategies (import substitution, export promotion)
Identify the problems of industrialization in Nigeria
Explain the roles of small and medium scale enterprises in development

topics.name: Natural Resources and the Nigerian Economy

subtopics.name: Petroleum and Other Mineral Resources
objectives: Identify Nigeria's major natural resources and their locations
Explain the contributions of petroleum and gas to the Nigerian economy
Explain the roles of OPEC and NNPC
Explain the negative effects of over-dependence on oil (Dutch disease, environmental degradation)

subtopics.name: Manufacturing and Service Sectors
objectives: Describe the contributions of manufacturing and services to the Nigerian economy
Explain the linkages between agriculture, industry and services

subtopics.name: Private Business Organizations
objectives: Describe the features, advantages and disadvantages of sole proprietorship and partnership
Describe private and public limited liability companies and cooperative societies
Distinguish between shares, debentures and bonds and methods of financing business

subtopics.name: Public Enterprises and Privatization
objectives: State the reasons for establishing public enterprises and their problems
Explain privatization and commercialization: reasons, benefits and problems
Explain indigenization and its objectives in Nigeria

subtopics.name: Population Theories, Structure and Distribution
objectives: Explain population concepts: size, growth rate, census, density and distribution
Explain the Malthusian and demographic transition theories of population
Analyse the structure of Nigeria's population (age, sex, occupational and geographical distribution)
Explain over-population, under-population and optimum population

subtopics.name: Labour Market and Unemployment
objectives: Explain the concepts of labour force, efficiency and mobility of labour
Explain the determination of wages and the roles of trade unions
Identify types, causes and effects of unemployment and its remedies in Nigeria

subtopics.name: Basis and Theory of International Trade
objectives: Distinguish between internal and international trade
Explain absolute and comparative advantage/comparative cost theory
State the advantages and disadvantages of international trade
Explain protectionism: tariffs, quotas and their effects

subtopics.name: Balance of Payments and Exchange Rates
objectives: Distinguish between balance of trade and balance of payments
Explain balance of payments disequilibrium: causes and corrective measures
Explain exchange rate systems (fixed, flexible) and devaluation and its effects
Explain the terms of trade and their measurement

subtopics.name: Global Economic Organizations
objectives: Describe the objectives and functions of the IMF, World Bank and WTO
Explain the roles of these organizations in developing economies
Describe the objectives of OPEC and Nigeria's membership benefits

subtopics.name: Regional Economic Organizations
objectives: Describe the objectives and achievements of ECOWAS, AU/AfDB and ECA
Explain the benefits and problems of economic integration in West Africa
